{{verse|chapter=7|verse=17}} And vvhen the time drevv neere of the promi{{ls}}{{ls}}e vvhich God had promi{{ls}}ed to Abraham, the people {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 1, 7.''}}* increa{{ls}}ed and vvas multiplied in Ægypt, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=18}} vntil an other king aro{{ls}}e in Ægypt, that knevv not Io{{ls}}eph. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=19}} This {{ls}}ame circumuenting our {{ls}}tocke, afflicted our fathers: that they {{ls}}hould expo{{ls}}e their children, to the end they might not be kept aliue. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=20}} The {{ls}}ame time vvas {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 2, 2.''}}* Moy{{ls}}es borne, and he vvas acceptable to God, who was nouri{{ls}}hed three moneths in his fathers hou{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=21}} And vvhen he vvas expo{{ls}}ed, Pharaos daughter tooke him vp, and nouri{{ls}}hed him for her ovvne {{ls}}onne. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=22}} And Moy{{ls}}es vvas in{{ls}}tructed in al the vvi{{ls}}edom of the Ægyptians: and he vvas mightie in his vvordes and vvorkes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=23}} And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 2, 11.''}}* vvhen he vvas fully of the age of fourtie yeres, it came to his minde to vi{{ls}}ite his brethren the children of Israël. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=24}} And vvhen he had {{ls}}een one {{ls}}uffer vvrong, he defended him: and {{ls}}triking the Ægyptian, he reuenged his quarel that {{ls}}u{{ls}}teined the vvrong. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=25}} And he thought that his brethren did vnder{{ls}}tand that God by his hand vvould {{ls}}aue them: but they vnder{{ls}}toode it not. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=26}} And the day folovving {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 2, 13.''}}* he appeared to them being at {{ls}}trife: and he reconciled them vnto peace, {{ls}}aying, Men, ye are brethren, vvherfore hurt you one an other?
